newsitem.title: GREECE: ING BARINGS LAUNCHES CALL WARRANTS ON GREEK STOCKS.
newsitem.headline: ING BARINGS LAUNCHES CALL WARRANTS ON GREEK STOCKS.

text.p: ING Barings is launching one-year, drachma denominated, American-style call warrants on a basket of six Greek blue chip stocks with Signa Securities and National Mortgage Bank acting as Greek placing agents, it said in a statement.
The call warrants will have a notional amount of 4.0 billion drachmas and an offering price of 14.50 percent, it said.
"Each warrant controls 10,000 drachmas of the underlying basket and the minimum trading size is 500 warrrants," it said.

The basket will be made up of OTE with a 30 percent weight, Hellenic Bottling Co with 20 percent, National Bank of Greece and Alpha Credit Bank with 17.5 percent each, Titan with 10 percent and National Mortgage Bank with 5.0 percent, it said.

The strike price remains to be determined and will be equal to the initial spot reference which is based on the arithmetic average of the drachma offer prices of the reference basket components over February 12 through 14, it said.

The warrants will be listed in Luxemburg and give investors exposure to a selected portfolio of blue-chip stocks while avoiding the costs of custody and settlement arrangements, it added. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
